findings.title: KeyError crash when Integration metadata has no 'sender'
findings.body: GitHubInstallation.dispatch accesses `integration.metadata["sender"]["login"]` directly. Any Integration row whose metadata lacks a 'sender' key will raise an unhandled KeyError and return a 500 to the user instead of the error page. This is reachable in at least two ways: (1) GitHub integrations created before this change (or by any path that didn't record a sender, e.g. a missed/partial installation webhook) have no 'sender' in metadata; (2) both Integration lookups (`Integration.objects.get(external_id=installation_id)` at line 477 and the second lookup at line 494) are not filtered by provider, so an ACTIVE integration from a different provider whose external_id happens to collide with the GitHub installation id will be fetched and its metadata (which never contains 'sender') will be dereferenced. The lookup should filter on provider='github' and use metadata.get('sender', {}).get('login') with a defined failure policy.

findings.title: User verification is skipped when the Integration row doesn't exist yet
findings.body: The installer-identity check (comparing the OAuth-authenticated GitHub user with metadata['sender']['login']) only runs on the branch where an Integration row already exists (i.e. the installation webhook has already been processed). When `Integration.DoesNotExist` is raised, dispatch goes straight to `pipeline.next_step()`, and the pipeline later creates the integration via build_integration with no sender and no verification at all. Since webhook delivery is asynchronous and not guaranteed, there is a race window (or a permanent gap, if the webhook is dropped) in which anyone who knows an installation_id can complete the Sentry-side setup for a GitHub installation they did not perform — exactly the scenario this PR is meant to prevent. The verification should not depend on the webhook having already created the Integration row.

findings.title: Unhandled exceptions from token exchange and get_user_info cause 500s
findings.body: In OAuthLoginView.dispatch, `safe_urlopen(...)` (line 423) and `get_user_info(payload["access_token"])` (line 434) are called without try/except. Network errors from safe_urlopen, non-2xx responses, or an ApiError raised by get_user_info when GitHub rejects the token will propagate and produce an unhandled 500 on a user-facing, attacker-influenceable endpoint (an attacker controls whether the `code` is valid or replayed). Only the happy-path failures (missing access_token in body, missing 'login' key) are handled; exceptions should be caught and routed to the same error() page.

findings.title: GitHub App install flow now hard-depends on GitHub OAuth app credentials being configured
findings.body: OAuthLoginView unconditionally calls `ghip.get_oauth_client_id()` / `get_oauth_client_secret()` and redirects to the OAuth authorize URL. Previously, installing the GitHub App did not require the separate GitHub OAuth App options to be set. On deployments (notably self-hosted) where the GitHub App is configured but the OAuth client id/secret options are empty, the installation flow will now redirect users to a GitHub authorize URL with a blank client_id (GitHub shows an error page) or fail when the provider raises on missing credentials, breaking all new GitHub integration installs. There is no feature flag or fallback for this new dependency.

findings.title: test_installation_not_found no longer exercises the installation-not-found (404) path
findings.body: The rewritten test uses a hardcoded state of 'ddd023d87a913d5226e2a882c4c4cc05', which differs from the pipeline signature '9cae5e88803f35ed7970fc131e6e65d3' used by every other test with an equivalent flow. The request therefore fails at the state-mismatch check in OAuthLoginView and renders the generic 'Invalid installation request.' error, so the assertion passes without ever reaching build_integration. The `responses.replace(..., status=404)` stub for /app/installations/{id} is now dead code, and the specific 'The GitHub installation could not be found.' error message from the 404 branch (which the old test asserted) is no longer covered by any test.
